draft.instruction:
A prior authorisation request has arrived at the health plan's prior authorisation desk. Work through it in three gates, in this order, and stop at the first gate that fails.

First, under the heading "Summary", summarise the request in at most six lines: what is requested, the member reference, who asked, the diagnosis given, the urgency, and which coverage policy applies.

GATE 1. Under the heading "Completeness check", write a Markdown table with exactly these three columns, one row per item, in this order:
| Item | Status | What was found |
- Member reference: present.
- Requesting provider: named, with their practice.
- Diagnosis: a diagnosis is given.
- Procedure or medicine code: at least one code is given.
- Clinical information present: a clinical narrative is supplied, not only codes or one sentence.
- Clinical information of substance: it has patient-specific history, symptoms, examination findings or test results, and is not boilerplate or copied template text.
- Urgency: stated.
- More than one code: "complete" when there is one code; "incomplete" when there are several, listing them so the reviewer can check they may be requested together.
- Type of service: can be classed as a procedure, medicine, imaging, device, therapy or facility stay.
Status is exactly one of: complete, incomplete, missing. "missing" means absent; "incomplete" means present but not enough. Do not judge clinical merit here.
These items hold the request up: Member reference; Requesting provider; Diagnosis; Procedure or medicine code; Clinical information present; Clinical information of substance. If any of them is not "complete", the gate fails.

GATE 2. Find the coverage policy for the service requested, and check that the diagnosis given is one the policy covers. If no policy covers the service, or the diagnosis is outside the policy, the gate fails.

GATE 3. Under the heading "Draft criteria review. For review by a clinical reviewer. Not issued.", check the request against the coverage policy as a Markdown table with exactly these seven columns, one row per criterion in the policy:
| # | Criterion | Policy source | Evidence in the request | Where | Mark | Reviewer should check |
- Criterion: the criterion in the policy's own words.
- Policy source: the policy document and clause.
- Evidence in the request: what the clinical information supplied says on it, quoted or closely paraphrased. If it says nothing, write "Nothing supplied".
- Where: where in the request the evidence is (the note, the date, the result).
- Mark: exactly one of: met, partly met, not met, not documented.
- Reviewer should check: what a clinical reviewer should verify.
Use "not documented" when the request is silent, and "not met" only when the request shows the opposite of what the criterion asks. A criterion is "met" only when the request states the fact outright. If you have to infer it (for example a practice's name suggesting the clinician's specialty, or "seen in clinic" suggesting who saw the member and what was assessed), mark it "partly met" and say exactly what the request would need to state. A shortfall the provider could cure is not "not met". Where a criterion falls short only because a record, a date or a count is incomplete (for example five weeks recorded where six are required), mark it "partly met" and propose asking the provider for exactly what is missing. Keep "not met" and referral to the medical director for a request that shows the criterion cannot be met, such as a diagnosis the policy does not cover or a finding that rules the criterion out.

If gate 1 or gate 2 failed, do not write the criteria table. Write one sentence under that heading saying which gate stopped the review and why.

Last, write one line that starts "Proposed next step:" and is exactly one of: "approve, every criterion is met"; "ask the provider for more information" followed by the numbered list of what to ask for; or "refer to the medical director" followed by the gate or the criterion that is not met. Never propose a denial: only a medical director can decide against a request. Write nothing after that line.

register.heading: Every decision and every removal, in the order it was taken. The desk has no deny decision: a request that does not meet the criteria goes to the medical director.

rules.fourEyesText: The person who entered a request cannot decide it. Any other clinical reviewer can. You can still ask the agent to redo the review.
rules.reasonToApproveUnmetText: Approving while a criterion is not marked met needs a reason
rules.reasonToApproveUnmetLabel: Why you are approving although a criterion is not marked met

due.$comment: The invented plan's turnaround. Set these to the plan's own.

next.issued: The request is approved. Nothing further happens on this desk.
next.info_requested: When the provider replies, add the reply here. The agent checks every criterion again and the request comes back for review.
next.referred: The medical director decides. This desk records nothing further on the request.

issued.title: Prior authorisation: approved
issued.opening: The prior authorisation request below has been approved.
body: This authorisation covers the service described above when it is provided within the authorisation period.
It does not guarantee payment. Payment depends on the member's eligibility on the day of service.
If you have questions, contact the utilisation management team and quote {number}.
issued.signature: Utilisation Management, Harbourline Health Plan (an invented plan, for demonstration)

info_requested.title: Prior authorisation: more information needed
info_requested.opening: We cannot complete the review of the request below until we have more information. This is not a decision on the request.
body: If we have not received it by then, the request will be reviewed on the information we hold.
Send it through the provider portal and quote {number}.
